action.subject: Edie
action.detail: hemp knot-cord bound with brass wire ferrules
action.note: Outline-mandated override in ch. 16: the cord turns up in Lloyd's own hands inside the delirium, counting to ninety-one (Edie's sapper number, which canon confirms she never told him) instead of the nineteen the ch. 2-3 search actually ran. Both counts agree and he trusts neither — the discrepancy is never resolved on the page, per outline. This is the cord as a load-bearing delirium image, not an incidental prop; let it rest well past ch. 16 before using it casually again.

action.note: Used again in ch. 12, one chapter after ch. 11 (min_gap 4) — second cooldown breach alongside the cord itself. Rested through ch. 13-18 as planned. Ch. 19 gives it its biggest scene yet: Edie tallies the whole Vantry job in it, line by line, and leaves it behind with the party for good ('for the next one') — the object's own arc now closed, title-echoing ('paid out'). Treat as retired as a recurring prop; if it reappears, it should be in someone else's hands, not Edie's.

action.subject: Ascension House
action.detail: a grand front entrance nobody uses, grass between the flags, against an oiled service door worked constantly by cart traffic
action.note: Used again ch. 15 as part of the escape route, now incidentally — Ascension House is destroyed by chapter's end, so this motif is effectively retired going forward.

action.subject: Vantry
action.detail: gaslamps lit at noon under a soot-haze that never fully lifts
action.note: Used again ch. 15, seen from the yard lit orange by the fire from underneath for the first time — a deliberate one-off variation on the recurring haze, not a plain repeat. The party stayed in Vantry's mill district through ch. 17-19 rather than leaving after ch. 15 as once assumed, so this is live again, not dormant: ch. 19 has Maria watch the lamps come up early over the better streets from the rented room, soot-haze or not, and use their punctuality as a trigger for her private arithmetic about who's at dinner in Carrowgate. They do leave Vantry for Carrowgate between ch. 19 and ch. 20 — retire as dormant from ch. 20 onward unless the plot returns to Vantry.

action.subject: Maria
action.detail: the intake register, kept wrapped and hidden, Anse Duley's name read and reread
action.note: Left Maria's hands for good in ch. 18 — handed to Edie for the broadsheet plates, then publicly called a likely forgery by people who hadn't read it. Retired as a physical object in Maria's possession; the floorboard space it left behind is reused once more in ch. 18 (now holding Vail's letter instead) but the register itself does not return.

action.subject: Ascension House extraction theatre
action.detail: a wall of case files, sixty years deep, each folder a name and a dated result of failure
action.note: Published in ch. 18 as a column of names run alongside the register plates, then shelved as a bound back-issue volume almost no one asks for by the chapter's end. Ch. 19 gives it the glancing reference anticipated last time — Maria reads, in a broadsheet, that the bound volume has gone to the Vantry assembly's standing archive, where nothing of its kind draws a second look once the story about it has aged. Retire this entry now; the image has done its full arc, from wall to volume to unread shelf.

action.subject: Maria
action.detail: a small flame held steady over her own palm, used as a plain light source rather than a weapon
action.note: Introduced ch. 15 — deliberately the least dramatic use of her Arcana in the siege and the most useful. Worth a return in a later high-tension Act III scene as a contrast to the lightning/fire she hates using, but not soon. Still dormant after ch. 19, a quiet connective chapter with no call for Arcana at all.

action.subject: Maria
action.detail: Vail's letter, warm and without reproach, kept folded under the floorboard in the exact space the intake register left behind
action.note: Introduced ch. 18 as the chapter's closing image — Maria neither answers nor burns it. Ch. 19 returns to it once, in the chapter's private, unspoken section. Ch. 22 confirms it stayed behind when they left Vantry for Carrowgate: she thinks of it, once, as a possible lever against Crane — going back to the Church after all — and sets the thought down almost as fast as it arrives, unused. Still a live Chekhov's object, now at a physical remove from the party as well as an emotional one. Don't resolve its fate off-page.

action.subject: Lloyd
action.detail: a session calendar matched against a watch roster, and a traced floor plan with three doors marked by neat crosses, carried folded inside his coat lining
action.note: Introduced ch. 20 as what Maria finds in his coat. Ch. 21 used it again exactly as anticipated. Ch. 22 keeps it on the table through all three days of the argument — still weighted flat under the candle stub, an unmoving fixture of the room rather than a fresh beat — and the chapter closes on it once more as the image she returns to after deciding to stay. Still expected again in ch. 24 when Edie independently reconstructs his reconnaissance from marks on a floor plan she finds in the building itself — check whether that one is this same sheet (carried on him) or a second working copy before drafting. Given how much work this single prop has now done, let it rest as plain set-dressing for a chapter or two unless ch. 23-24 need it moved again.

action.subject: Lloyd
action.detail: pale, fine dust off dressed stone ground into a boot toe, distinct from coal-yard soot
action.note: Introduced ch. 20 as the single physical tell that starts Maria's suspicion before she has anything else to go on — government-building stone against a coal-yard man's boots. A small, literal clue rather than a mood image; hold it in reserve for a later chapter where it could pay off again (confirming a lie, say) rather than spending it as plain texture.

character.subject: Edie
character.detail: thick oilcloth ledger
character.note: Ch. 19 — Edie closes the account she's kept in it for the whole Vantry job and leaves it with Maria and Lloyd on departing for Carrowgate. Ch. 22 confirms the prediction made at the time: it reappears in someone else's hands, not Edie's. Maria goes through it alone on the third day, looking for a way to make Crane's dry figures carry the same weight the Vantry registers once did, and finds the opposite lesson instead — a story already called a forgery poisons the next one. Functions here as a prop for her reasoning rather than a recurring sensory image; no need to force it back into rotation unless the plot gives her a reason to open it again.

character.subject: Lloyd
character.detail: counts something concrete to manage a fact he can't otherwise process
character.note: Outline-mandated early reuse in ch. 16, one chapter ahead of the ch. 17 hold set last time — the knot-cord counted twice in the delirium, both counts agreeing at ninety-one and trusted by Lloyd anyway. Not a free choice; the beat is written into ch. 16's outline entry. Push the hold further out this time: avoid until at least ch. 20.

character.subject: Lloyd
character.detail: half-inch gap in the roof at his mother's house in Callow Ford, daylight showing through the north gable
character.note: First given to Maria as a told-not-shown detail in ch. 6; surfaces again in ch. 16 as the image Lloyd's delirium keeps sliding back to underneath the other two stairs, and the chapter ends on it. A strong candidate for a deliberate, earned return in ch. 25 when Maria actually reaches Callow Ford — hold it dormant until then rather than spending it incidentally.

character.subject: Church buildings
character.detail: a loaf, a roof, and a pair of clasped hands carved over the door, worn soft by decades of hands

character.subject: Maria and Lloyd
character.detail: naming the plain objects of a room aloud — cup, window, blanket, a hand — to tell him what's real
character.note: Introduced ch. 16 as Maria's voice reaching Lloyd from outside his delirium; reciprocated ch. 17 from her side, now explicitly a standing habit carried over from the Salts rather than a one-off. Central to the ch. 17 climax (his 'is this real,' her answer built out of the same named objects). Core to the relationship — don't retire it, but let it rest a few chapters before leaning on it again so it keeps its weight for whenever his Insight or her faith is next in question.

character.subject: Lloyd
character.detail: a ridge of badly-knit bone above the wrist where Maria could argue the break straight but not re-set it clean, catching for a half-second before the fist closes
character.note: A new mark from the ch. 15 siege injuries (right arm broken in three places), healed in stages in ch. 17 — distinct from the ch. 3/ch. 6 elbow wrongness tracked separately as 'crooked-arm' (still resting until ch. 25; do not conflate the two images or use the old 'five-degree angle' phrasing for this one). This is the first physical cost Maria names herself as directly responsible for causing, not just failing to prevent.

character.subject: Maria
character.detail: the floor plan and session calendar found in Lloyd's coat, held open too long to refold steadily along its own creases
character.note: Ch. 20's closing image — the shake in her hands is the chapter's one explicit tell of how hard the discovery has hit her. Ch. 21 brought it back out in dialogue. Ch. 22 is quieter with it: she doesn't touch it again, just registers that it hasn't moved from under the candle stub in three days, a fixture rather than a fresh discovery now that the argument has moved past the plan itself to what killing costs. Hold it dormant for a chapter unless ch. 23-24 need it in someone's hands again.

character.subject: Lloyd
character.detail: coal-yard day-wages counted out into small stacks on the table each evening, never explained and never asked about
character.note: New in ch. 22 — a quiet domestic habit distinct from the 'counting-tell' motif (which is Lloyd counting something concrete to manage a fact he can't otherwise process, currently resting). This one is plain household economy, not anxiety management, and Maria explicitly notes she's never asked why he does it. Worth a possible payoff later (what he's counted out for, or saving toward) rather than spending it as incidental texture again soon.

atmosphere.subject: Ascension House
atmosphere.detail: rows of brine tanks holding people who have never surfaced
atmosphere.note: The ch. 16 exception has now been used exactly as anticipated — Ivet surfacing in the second tank from the door, inside Lloyd's delirium, with the Insight ambiguity left fully open per canon. Ascension House burned in ch. 15; this image now belongs only to Lloyd's private delirium and should not recur as an ordinary physical-location motif. Retired.
